project_title: Climate Change Analysis: Exploring Connections Between Temperature and GHG Emissions
key_findings: Weak negative correlation between CO2 emissions and temperature change (r = -0.074, p = 0.025)
Global emissions increased 22.5% while average temperature increased 0.77°C
Small wealthy nations show highest temperature sensitivity per emission unit
Major emitters (USA, Russia, Japan) show relatively modest temperature increases
No significant regional patterns between European and non-European countries

hypothesis_results.H2: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED - Significant but weak correlation
hypothesis_results.H5: SUPPORTED - Both metrics show positive trends

main_conclusion: Climate change relationships are more complex than simple country-level emission-temperature correlations, supporting the need for global rather than local approaches to climate action.
